cohort: 104,065 pregnant women in Japan, enrolled in the Japan Environment and Children's Study (JECS)
finding: Vaginal delivery with anesthesia was associated with a higher risk of postpartum depression at six months after childbirth, compared with vaginal delivery without analgesia.
mod_finding: The risk of postpartum depression at six months after childbirth tended to be increased after vaginal delivery with anesthesia, compared with vaginal delivery without analgesia.
